Thanks Sophia — below are concise answers and where we'll provide evidence. Monica will follow up with the engineering note. If you want anything in writing for the SOW, we can add the exact retention windows and opt-out language.

Short answers (hosted API / default behaviour):
- What is stored: by default, the hosted Redwood API stores request payloads (prompts) and model outputs for 30 days to support quality monitoring and customer support. System metadata (timestamps, request ids) are kept with that data. Telemetry (metrics, aggregated usage) is retained separately and is not customer-identifiable unless configured.
- Logs & tracing: application logs do not store full prompts by default — prompts are stored in the request store described above. Traces contain request ids and latency metrics only.
- Retention options: standard hosted retention is 30 days; contract options commonly requested are 90 days or no retention (we can provide "no-storage" contractual language for an enterprise addendum; this requires Dedicated or Private deployment for strict enforcement).
- Residency and region: Hosted customers are stored in the region you select (we have us, eu, apac regions). If you need an account-level residency guarantee (EU-only or US-only), Dedicated or Private deployments are recommended; for hosted we can pin your storage to us-east-1 but contractual data residency controls are stronger on Dedicated/Private.
- KV cache & ephemeral state: KV caches for model acceleration are kept in memory and are not persisted to disk in our runtime. They are not part of the request store.
- Encryption & keys: data at rest is encrypted; customer-managed KMS keys are supported on Dedicated and Private; hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default.

Hi Sophia — Monica from Customer Success / Tech Ops here. A few technical clarifications to support procurement and engineering review:

1) Data fragments and storage locations
- Request store: raw prompts + model outputs are written to an encrypted object store in the configured region (e.g., us-east-1). By default the retention TTL is 30 days; object lifecycle policies permanently delete after TTL.
- KV cache: stored in RAM-backed processes for inference acceleration; not persisted to disk and not replicated to central long-term storage. If a node restarts, cache is reconstructed from upstream model context — there is no lasting cache artifact.

2) Logs & tracing
- Application logs include request ids and masked metadata by default. Full prompts are not emitted into tracing logs unless explicitly enabled for debug troubleshooting (option disabled in prod by default).
- Audit logs: access events (who fetched what) are retained; we can provide audit-log exports for Dedicated/Private with 365-day retention if required.

3) Encryption & access controls
- All data at rest is encrypted with AES-256; hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS. Dedicated/Private can be configured with customer-managed KMS/HSM.
- Role-based access controls limit who can access request-store objects; we provide both RBAC and fine-grained S3-style policies on Dedicated/Private.

4) Contractual opt-out
- If Cerebellum requires a contractual "no prompt retention" clause, we typically require Dedicated or Private deployment so the retention behavior can be enforced and independently audited. We can draft addendum language for procurement to review.

Attachments: redwood-technical-evidence-statement.pdf (engineering note with exact lifecycle and encryption details).

If you want an engineer on a short call to validate any of the above for procurement, happy to schedule.

Thanks,
